question: Which of the following characteristics will a patient with helminth infection and one who is responding to an allergen have in common ?:

options.opa: In both patients an increase of cytotoxic T lymphocytes will be detected.
options.opb: In both patients the innate immunity will be deficient.
options.opc: In both, an elevated level of serum IgE will be detected.
options.opd: Both patients have a high risk of developing an autoimmune disease.

analysis: Both helminth infections and allergic responses are associated with elevated levels of IgE. IgE is an antibody that plays a crucial role in the body's immune response to allergens and parasitic infections, particularly helminths. This is due to the activation of Th2 cells, which stimulate the production of IgE. Therefore, the common characteristic between a patient with a helminth infection and one responding to an allergen is the elevated level of serum IgE.
